correctness.rationale: Each log chord has a mean-zero L2 Fourier series with real cosine coefficients -1/k. Parseval gives V=one half sum |S_k|^2/k^2. The Bernoulli identity for angle differences of magnitude less than 2 pi makes V exactly quadratic on the ordered chamber, including its coincidence faces. In the expanded n-vector of angles, the quadratic part is n/4 times the centered squared displacement from the regular angles (the linear term is fixed by the derivative of the ordered absolute values), and the regular value is pi^2/12. Within a block of m successive regular angles the successive spacing is 2 pi/n, and the sum of squared residuals about its mean is pi^2 m(m^2-1)/(3n^2); the residuals have zero sum so no mixed terms with block shifts occur. This gives the exact angular defect, including arbitrary lifts by rotation and r=1. The successive midpoint gaps, including wraparound, are pi(m_j+m_{j+1})/n, positive and summing to 2 pi. Equality is precisely common rotation in each cyclic assignment, and the integer cubic exchange 3(a-b-1)(a+b)>0 proves the balanced-multiplicity minimum. An independent check is the exact circular transport reduction in the originality assessment. The frozen rational checker was inspected, not run; the composition tests are finite and not the proof.

The infimum subtracts the weighted mean of x_j-c_j; the remaining exact sum is sum p_j^3/12 plus the weighted centered square. Since c_j=phi_j^*/(2 pi)+1/(2n), multiplying by pi^2 n^2 recovers both terms of the frozen identity, all equality positions and cyclic gaps. Strict integer convexity gives the fixed-r consequence.
